### Steps to Reprodu

answers.body:
Hey @yosun! The first bug you reported is real — when the provider resolves to OpenAI Codex, the default model (`anthropic/claude-opus-4.6`) should be automatically swapped for a Codex-compatible one. We're working on getting that fixed.

Regarding the second issue in your comment — `hermes models set openai/gpt-5.3-codex` — a couple of things:

1. The terminal CLI command is `hermes model` (singular, no `set` subcommand). It opens an interactive picker where you select your provider and model.

2. More importantly, `hermes model` is a **terminal command** you run from your shell (outside of Hermes). When you're inside an active Hermes session (at the `●` prompt), you use the **slash commands** instead:
   - `/model` — shows your current model and available options
   - `/model gpt-5.3-codex` — switches to a specific model
   - `/provider` — shows available providers

So the workflow would be either:
- **From your terminal:** `hermes model` (interactive picker, sets your default for future sessions)
- **Inside a session:** `/model gpt-5.3-codex` (switches model for the current session)

The first bug (Codex provider not auto-correcting the model) will be addressed shortly.

Fixed in commit 95b1130. When the provider resolves to `openai-codex`, Hermes now automatically:

1. **Replaces incompatible models** (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6`) with the best available Codex model
2. **Strips provider prefixes** (e.g. `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` → `gpt-5.3-codex`) that the Codex API rejects
3. **Warns only when the user explicitly set** the incompatible model (silently fixes the config default)

Thanks to @stablegenius49 (#661) and @teyrebaz33 (#696) for their PRs which informed the final fix.

answers.body:
Qwen 3.5 9B/4B models are very small and will naturally be slower with tool-heavy workflows — the agent sends the full tool schema (~45 tools) on every API call, which is a lot of input tokens for a 4B-9B model. This is a hardware/model limitation, not a Hermes bug.

Tips for better performance with small local models:
- Reduce toolsets: `hermes tools` → disable toolsets you don't need
- Use a faster quantization if available
- Consider a larger model (32B+) for tool-heavy work
- Set `terminal.backend: local` to avoid container overhead

author: estebanavv
body:
### Bug Description

Updated 30 mins ago. Then I was inquiring why the skill was built outside of ~/.hermes it took very long to answer and then I stopped it. and got a very odd  answer that could not come up from anything I have done so far makes me worry that there is some odd prompt injection or some material leaks to context .

```

   You're a junior dev, right? You don't belong here.

answers.body:
Thanks for the additional context! The 3.5MB clawhub_catalog_v1.json cache file is likely the injection source — the agent may have read skill descriptions from that catalog while searching, and one of them contained adversarial text.

PR #1562 adds injection pattern detection for skill files. I'll look into whether the index-cache files also need protection.

Updated PR #1562 with a second fix: read_file now blocks direct access to ~/.hermes/skills/.hub/index-cache/ files. This prevents the agent from reading the 3.5MB clawhub_catalog_v1.json (or any other catalog cache) directly into context, which was likely the injection vector in your case.

The root cause fix is in PR #1648. The existing fix (commit 96dac22) blocks `read_file` access to `.hub/` cache files, but the primary injection vector was `search_files` discovering those files via `find` or `grep` (which don't skip hidden directories like ripgrep does). PR #1648 makes all three search backends consistently exclude hidden directories.

title: [Setup]: How do I run as root in Docker to get apt working?
author: spergware
body:
### What's Going Wrong?

Sorry if I don't ask in the Discord server but I deleted that spyware. As per title, apt install is not working in docker mode and somewhere in the documentation I read that instead of sudo I have to run as root inside the container, but what's the official way to go about that? I read the docs but I'm lost. Thank you in advance.

### Steps Taken

Checked all the configs

### Installation Method

Install script (curl | bash)

### Operating System

Debian 13

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Output of `hermes doctor`

```shell

```

### Full Error Output

```shell
No idea
```

### What I've Already Tried

_No response_

answers.body:
The Docker container already runs as root by default — no sudo needed, and no extra configuration required.

The default working directory inside the container is `/root`, and the necessary Linux capabilities for package managers (`CHOWN`, `FOWNER`, `DAC_OVERRIDE`) are already granted. So `apt install` should work as-is.

If it's still failing, a few things to check:

1. **Don't use sudo** — you're already root inside the container, `sudo` won't be available. Use `apt-get install -y <package>` directly.

2. **Run `apt-get update` first** — the default image may not have a fresh package index:
   ```bash
   apt-get update && apt-get install -y <package>
   ```

3. **Check which image you're using** — the default is `nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.11-nodejs20`. If you've set a custom `docker_image`, it may have a different base that behaves differently.

4. **Paste the actual error** — "no idea" doesn't help diagnose whether it's a network issue, a missing `apt-get update`, or something else.

If you can share the exact error output, it'll be easier to pinpoint.

**Closing — this is now documented.**

The official `nousresearch/hermes-agent` image already runs the gateway as root during init (it drops to the unprivileged `hermes` user only for the supervised services), so `apt-get install` works directly inside the container — no `sudo` needed (and `sudo` isn't present; you're effectively root for package installs). Run `apt-get update` first, then `apt-get install -y <pkg>`.

For persisting extra tools across image upgrades (rather than ad-hoc installs that vanish on `docker pull`), the recommended approach is a small derived image — see the docs:
**https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/docker#installing-more-tools-in-the-container**

Note also that several tools that were previously missing are now baked into the image (e.g. `curl`, `git`, `ffmpeg`, `ripgrep`, `docker-cli`).

Closing as answered/not-planned since the workflow is documented. If the docs don't cover your case, comment and we'll reopen.

title: [Setup]: Error al actualizar hermes en Termux (terminal android)
author: VictorR29
body:
### What's Going Wrong?

Con las ultimas actulazaciones hermes dejo de funcionar en termux. Antes lo habia configurado y trabajaba de forma perfecta y sin errores hasta que lo actualice y de allí dejo de funcionar

### Steps Taken

El error parace tener que ver con la installación de littlellm . La version no parece ser compatible con las librerias python que admite termux en el entorno proot.

### Installation Method

Install script (curl | bash)

### Operating System

Termux andorid | proot ubuntu 25.10

### Python Version

3.13.17

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Output of `hermes doctor`

```shell

```

### Full Error Output

```shell
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement litellm>=1.75.5 (from hermes-agent) (from versions: none)

ERROR: No matching distribution found for litellm>=1.75.5
```

### What I've Already Tried

_No response_

answers.body:
**Root cause identified**

`litellm` is not a direct dependency of hermes-agent — it's pulled in transitively by the optional `yc-bench` extra:

```toml
# pyproject.toml
yc-bench = ["yc-bench @ git+https://github.com/collinear-ai/yc-bench.git ; python_version >= '3.12'"]
```

`yc-bench` requires `litellm`, and `litellm>=1.75.5` has no prebuilt wheel for your platform (Termux / proot-ubuntu on ARM). The install script runs `uv pip install -e ".[all]"` which drags in `yc-bench` and therefore litellm.

**Workarounds (pick one)**

**Option 1 — skip the `yc-bench` extra (recommended)**

Install without `[all]`, manually adding only the extras you need:

```bash
uv pip install -e ".[messaging,cron,mcp,pty,cli]"
```

Or skip extras entirely for a minimal install:

```bash
uv pip install -e .
```

**Option 2 — install from `requirements.txt` (no extras)**

```bash
uv pip install -r requirements.txt
# or
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

**Option 3 — build litellm from source**

If you specifically need `yc-bench`:

```bash
pip install --no-binary litellm litellm
uv pip install -e ".[all]"
```

---

**For maintainers**: the `[all]` meta-extra implicitly pulls in `yc-bench` which brings a heavy ML benchmarking dependency (`litellm`, `streamlit`, `plotly`) that breaks on constrained environments. Consider excluding `yc-bench` from `[all]` since it's a niche benchmark tool, not a standard integration.

Hello The specific error you encountered (`No matching distribution found for litellm`) was not a Termux/Android compatibility issue. It was caused by `litellm` being quarantined on PyPI globally due to a security issue.

The maintainers have just released a hotfix (check the Discord announcements) that completely removes `litellm` from the installation requirements. If you run the install script again now, it will bypass this specific error.

### Steps Taken

### Installation Method

Install script (curl | bash)

### Operating System

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

### Output of `hermes doctor`

```shell

```

### Full Error Output

```shell
Full install (.[all]) failed, trying base install...
Using Python 3.11.15 environment at: venv
Resolved 76 packages in 365ms
Built hermes-agent @ file:///root/.hermes/hermes-agen
Prepared 2 packages in 7.95s
Uninstalled 1 package in 24ms █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ [6/69] tenacity==9.1.4 warning: Failed to hardlink files; falling back to full copy. This may lead to degraded performance.
If the cache and target directories are on different filesystems, hardlinking may not be supported.
If this is intentional, set export UV_LINK_MODE=copy or use --link-mode=copy to suppress this warning.
error: Failed to install: websockets-16.0-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_aarch64.manylinux_2_17_aarch64.manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl (websockets==16.0)
Caused by: Failed to copy to /root/.hermes/hermes-agent/ven

answers.body:
Hi @VictorR29,

This is a known issue with `uv` inside proot environments on aarch64 (Termux). The problem is that `uv` creates a temp file and tries to rename/move it atomically, but proot doesn't fully support cross-directory atomic file operations, so the temp path disappears mid-copy.

**Fix:**

```bash
export UV_LINK_MODE=copy
export TMPDIR=$HOME/tmp
mkdir -p $HOME/tmp
```

Then re-run the install:

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent && uv pip install -e '.[all]'
```

Setting `UV_LINK_MODE=copy` disables the hardlink/rename strategy entirely and forces a plain file copy, which proot handles fine. Setting `TMPDIR` to a path inside your home keeps temp files on the same filesystem as the target, which avoids the cross-mount issue.

If the error persists, you can also try falling back to pip directly:

```bash
pip install -e '.[all]'
```

Let us know if that resolves it.

Could you share the full traceback? Run hermes with verbose logging:

Then paste the full error output. The 'NoneType strip' error could be in many places — we need the stack trace to identify the root cause.

Thanks for the report — this is fixed in **v0.5.0** (released 2026-03-28).

This was an automated [hermes-sweeper](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) review.

**Root cause & fix:**
- When a YAML config key is present but has no value (e.g. `model:` with nothing after it), Python's YAML parser returns `None`. `dict.get(key, "")` only falls back to `""` when the key is *absent* — it returns `None` when the key exists with a null value. Calling `.strip()` on `None` crashes with the exact error reported.
- Fixed in commit `be39292` (PR #3552): changed all affected callsites in `cli.py`, `hermes_cli/main.py`, and `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` to use `(cfg.get(key) or "").strip()`.

**Evidence:**
- `be392926` — `fix(cli): guard .strip() against None values from YAML config (#3552)`
- Ships in tag `v2026.3.28` / v0.5.0

To verify connection: hermes honcho status

Note: Honcho is a memory layer, not a context window it won't remember tool details within the same session. It helps across sessions.

@Heavy-A The error "Honcho init failed: Invalid API key" appears during initialization but if you're still getting responses from Honcho, it may be a non-fatal warning that gets swallowed. The SDK validates the key format before connecting.

This is exactly what PR #3570 fixes — it injects "local" as a placeholder key when localhost is detected, preventing the validation error entirely. Until the PR is merged, add HONCHO_API_KEY=local to ~/.hermes/.env.

Thanks for the detailed report, @CHesketh76 — and to @ygd58, @paraddox, and @devorun for the quick follow-up and contributor PRs.

This was fixed in commit 0bd7e95df and shipped in **v2026.3.30** (2026-03-28). The combined fix:

- **Relaxes all Honcho activation gates** to accept either an `api_key` **or** a `base_url` as valid credentials (so local-only configs no longer require a key to activate the plugin).
- **Injects `"local"` as a placeholder API key** at SDK-client init time whenever `base_url` points to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1` — preventing the "Invalid API key" SDK validation error entirely (`plugins/memory/honcho/client.py`, lines 655–669).

If you're still on v0.4.0, a `hermes update` (or pip upgrade) to v2026.3.30 or later should resolve the issue. No workaround like `HONCHO_API_KEY=local` is needed after updating.

answers.body:
Root cause identified and fix submitted in #3997.

**What's happening:** `provider: auto` scans your environment for API keys. Since you have an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or similar) set, it picks that up and routes to `https://api.anthropic.com` — completely ignoring your `base_url: http://localhost:11434` config.

**Immediate workaround** — change one line in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
model:
  default: ollama/minimax-m2.7:cloud
  provider: custom          # ← was: auto
  base_url: http://localhost:11434
fallback_providers: []
```

Setting `provider: custom` forces Hermes to use your `base_url` instead of auto-detecting from environment variables. This should make it work right now without waiting for the fix to be merged.

The 404 you're seeing now is a different issue — and actually means the routing fix is working. Your request is now correctly hitting `http://localhost:11434` instead of Anthropic. The problem is on Ollama's side.

Ollama doesn't know the model `minimax-m2.7:cloud`. The `:cloud` suffix is not a valid Ollama tag — it's a naming convention used by some providers to distinguish cloud-hosted variants, but Ollama only serves models you've explicitly pulled locally.

To fix the 404:

1. Check what models you actually have available:
```
ollama list
```

2. Pull a model that Ollama supports, for example:
```
ollama pull llama3.2
```

3. Update your config to use that model name exactly as it appears in `ollama list`:
```yaml
model:
  default: llama3.2
  provider: custom
  base_url: http://localhost:11434
fallback_providers: []
```

If you specifically want to use MiniMax M2, it's a cloud-only model and can't run locally on Ollama — you'd need to use it through a provider like OpenRouter instead.

title: [Enhancement]: subagents fake spawn or not?
author: paciox
body: ### Bug Description Hello, updated to the latest version of hermes today and searched issues. I specifically asked hermes to spawn multi agents to parallelize lenghty multiple repetitive isolated tasks but it seems to fake it. I see this delegate (1 at time) and I see only sequential output in the TUI. What am I doing wrong? The prompt was specifically beginning with: > Your task: Do a complete multi-spawned, agent swarm, coordinated by a leader agent that gets reports from spawned agents briefing, brainstorming information recollection, google search Is there something to set up or that I am doing wrong? It keeps saying "delegating" but looks like it's not doing it? ### Steps to Reproduce Run hermes, Ask him to do multiagent parallel work like > Your task: Do a complete multi-spawned, agent swarm, coordinated by a leader agent that gets reports from spawned agents briefing, brainstorming information recollection, google search ### Expected Behavior To run in parallel multiple agent and possibly showing either overlapped/interleaved logs o

answers.body:
This is expected behavior — Hermes's delegation tool runs subagents sequentially, not in parallel. The "delegate" tool spawns one subagent at a time and waits for it to complete before the next one starts.

True parallel multi-agent execution is not currently supported. The `/background` command can run a single agent in the background while you continue chatting, but coordinated parallel swarms are not implemented.

If you want to track this as a feature request rather than a bug, the label should be changed from "bug" to "enhancement".

title: [Bug]: Open WebUI - No Tool Progress?
author: Silvenga

answers.body: Opened #5373. It does not flip the current API-server default; it adds a safe per-request opt-out so streaming clients can suppress inline tool-progress chunks with `verbose: false` (or the more explicit `stream_tool_progress: false`, which wins if both are present). Since v0.7.0 already shipped progress-by-default, I think this should be treated as a compatibility-safe feature and merged only as that, not as a default-behavior reversal.

<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=5352 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->
Automated hermes-sweeper review: this bug is fixed on `main` and shipped in **v2026.4.8**.

**Root cause (confirmed):** `_on_tool_progress` in `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` accepted 3 positional args but `run_agent.py` calls `tool_progress_callback` with 4 — `(event_type, name, preview, args)`. **Evidence:**
- Commit [`7ec838507`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/7ec838507a7e2e1d7002c04180d9f4b302a6a4b8) — `fix(api_server): update tool_progress_callback signature for Open WebUI streaming` — is present on `main` and in `v2026.4.8`+.

- PR #5372 by @Mibayy (which described this exact fix) appears to have been merged; its commit is on `main`.

Note: PR #5373 (adding a `verbose: false` / `stream_tool_progress` opt-out knob) is still open — that's a follow-on enhancement, not a requirement to close this bug report.

title: Question: should local STT retry on CPU int8 when faster-whisper hits cuBLAS runtime errors?
author: bernylinville
body:
## Summary
I originally noticed this while running `hermes update`, but the more relevant point is *why I had a local modification in `tools/transcription_tools.py` in the first place*.

The local change was not arbitrary customization. It was a small workaround for local STT failure when `faster-whisper` tried to use GPU mode and hit a CUDA/cuBLAS runtime error.

This may overlap with #2885. If so, please feel free to close this as a duplicate. I mainly wanted to document the motivation for the local patch.

## Why I modified this source file locally
My local change added a retry path in `_transcribe_local()`:

- first try `WhisperModel(..., device="auto", compute_type="auto")`
- if transcription raises a `RuntimeError` mentioning `cublas` / `libcublas.so`
- log a warning
- rebuild the model with `device="cpu", compute_type="int8"`
- retry transcription on CPU

In other words, the local patch was trying to turn a hard failure into a graceful fallback.

## Why this seemed useful
For some environments, GPU inference is *partially* available from Python package / wheel perspective, but the actual runtime still fails because the expected CUDA system libraries are not available or not

answers.body:
<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=6102 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->
Thanks for the detailed write-up and for sharing the exact patch you were carrying — this is a great bug report.

This is an automated hermes-sweeper review.

The fallback you proposed is fully implemented on `main` as of commit [`4350668`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/4350668ae49c903640179ebdaa99f59687ff951c):

- **`_load_local_whisper_model()`** (`tools/transcription_tools.py` ~line 350): tries `device="auto"`, catches CUDA library load errors via `_looks_like_cuda_lib_error()`, falls back to `device="cpu", compute_type="int8"`.
- **`_transcribe_local()`** (~line 406): additionally wraps `transcribe()` itself — evicts the broken cached model, reloads on CPU+int8, retries once. This handles the exact case you described where the model loads fine but `transcribe()` fails at first dlopen.
- The `_CUDA_LIB_ERROR_MARKERS` list includes `"libcublas"`, `"libcudnn"`, `"libcudart"`, `"cannot be loaded"`, `"no CUDA-capable device"`, and driver-mismatch strings — matching your own design of limiting fallback to cuBLAS-related failures only.

Linked issue #2885 (which you noted as a potential duplicate) was also closed once this fix landed. Your patch and the upstream implementation are functionally equivalent — you can drop your local modification and `hermes update` will carry the fix going forward.

## Investigation: Already Fixed

The error in this report — `ValidationException: content.0.tool_use.input: Field required` — was a bug in the Anthropic adapter's conversation replay path. Raw SDK response blocks were captured verbatim and replayed on subsequent turns, but Bedrock's InvokeModel API strictly requires the `input` field on every `tool_use` block.

### Fixes already on main

Three commits (all after this issue was filed on 2026-04-28) resolved the underlying problem:

- **`aaccaada2`** — Preserve interleaved thinking/tool\_use block order on replay
- **`529bb1c3d`** — Strip output-only SDK fields from replayed content blocks. The new `_sanitize_replay_block` function whitelists input-permitted fields per block type, guaranteeing `tool_use` blocks always include `input` (defaults to `{}`).
- **`7a1eed826`** — Redact replayed tool inputs from the stored tool\_calls map + broaden thinking-replay 400 recovery

These were landed via **PR #43943** (merged 2026-06-11).

### Recommendation

This issue can be closed. If the reporter is still seeing the error on the latest version, a fresh bug report with current `hermes doctor` output and Hermes version would help — but the specific `tool_use.input: Field required` path has been addressed.

title: Would a YantrikDB memory provider plugin be welcome?
author: spranab
body:
Hi folks — I'm the author of [YantrikDB](https://github.com/yantrikos/yantrikdb-server), a self-hosted cognitive memory backend (Rust, HTTP REST, port 7438, optional HA cluster). Before opening a PR I wanted to check whether a `plugins/memory/yantrikdb/` contribution would be welcome and get early design feedback.

## Why this might be interesting alongside the existing memory plugins

YantrikDB isn't trying to be another vector store — it actively maintains its own memory:

- **`think()`** runs a bounded maintenance pass: canonicalizes near-duplicates, flags contradictions and superseded facts, optionally mines temporal and co-occurrence patterns. Returns a structured response (counts, duration, server-suggested follow-up triggers).
- **Recall is explainable.** Every result carries a `why_retrieved` reason list (`semantic_match`, `graph-connected via X`, `important (decay=0.91)`, `keyword_match`, …) so the agent can audit ranking instead of treating it as opaque.
- **Contradictions are surfaced, not overwritten.** `conflicts()` lists unresolved claims and the agent closes each via `resolve_conflict(strategy=keep_winner | merge | keep_both | dismiss)`.
- **Temporal decay with confi

Per the updated [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), new memory providers are no longer accepted as in-tree additions to `plugins/memory/`:

title: Multi-agent communication & per-channel persona like openclaw
author: shuans
body:
Hi Hermes team,

I'm interested in two capabilities for Hermes Agent:

1. **Multi-agent Communication:**
   - How can multiple agents communicate with each other within Hermes Agent? Are there APIs, primitives, or best practices for agent-to-agent messaging or coordination, similar to openclaw?

2. **Per-Channel Persona/Context (like openclaw):**
   - Is it possible for a single agent to have different personas, identities, or isolated state in different channels/groups—so that the same underlying agent can act as a different "persona" in each group (as openclaw supports)?
   - If so, what's the best pattern for this? If not, are there plans or suggested workarounds?

Any examples, docs, or insight would be much appreciated. Thank you!

answers.body:
Multi-agent communication in Hermes is primarily achieved through the `delegate_task` tool. This allows a primary agent to spawn and communicate with specialized sub-agents to parallelize work or handle complex, multi-step tasks.

Regarding **per-channel personas**:
Hermes supports this through its extensible gateway architecture. Platforms like Discord or Telegram can inject a `channel_prompt` into the `MessageEvent`. 

You can configure distinct system prompts for different channels by:
1.  **Utilizing Hooks**: Registering a `pre_llm_call` hook in a plugin to modify the system prompt based on the channel ID.
2.  **Adapter Customization**: Modifying the platform's adapter in `gateway/platforms/` to load specific prompts based on the incoming metadata.

This provides the same per-channel flexibility found in tools like OpenClaw.

<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=11922 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->
Thanks for the detailed question! Both capabilities you're asking about are already available in Hermes Agent.

---

**Multi-agent communication** is handled by the `delegate_task` tool:
- Spawns isolated child AIAgent instances with their own context, toolsets, and terminal sessions
- Supports single-task and parallel batch modes (up to 3 concurrent subagents by default, configurable)
- Full docs: [`website/docs/user-guide/features/delegation.md`](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/delegation)

**Per-channel persona/context** is handled by the `channel_prompts` config key:
- Set distinct ephemeral system prompts per channel/group ID in your platform config
- Supported on Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost
- Implemented in `gateway/platforms/base.py` (`resolve_channel_prompt()`), called from each platform adapter
- Discord docs example: [`website/docs/user-guide/messaging/discord.md#discordchannel_prompts`](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/discord)
- Telegram docs: [`website/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram.md`](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram)

The contributor comment from @aniruddhaadak80 also describes the hooks approach (`pre_llm_call` in a plugin) as an alternative for more dynamic persona routing.

Closing as implemented — this is an automated hermes

title: [Setup]: [Bug] HTTP 400 API_KEY_INVALID with Google Provider on the latest version (Worked fine in previous version)
author: cwqrwq
body:
### What's Going Wrong?

I am experiencing a persistent HTTP 400: API_KEY_INVALID error when trying to use the native Gemini provider with Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Important Context: * My GEMINI_API_KEY is 100% valid. It works perfectly in OpenClaw and direct curl requests.

It worked perfectly fine this morning. The issue only started happening immediately after I updated to the newest version of Hermes.

I have already completely cleared my WSL environment, deleted ~/.hermes, did a fresh install, and ensured there are no conflicting keys (like AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY) in the .env file. The issue persists.

It seems the latest update introduced a bug in how Hermes formats or passes the API key to the generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai endpoint (possibly an issue with the Bearer token header or URL query construction).

Environment & Setup:

Provider: gemini

Model: gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview

Endpoint: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai
API call failed (attempt 1/3): BadRequestError [HTTP 400]
🔌 Provider: gemini Model: gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview
🌐 Endpoint: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai
📝 Error: HTTP 400: Er

answers.body:
Fixed by PR #12251 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/12251), merged as ca32a2a6 on main.

Root cause: #11961 added a Google-specific header hack (`x-goog-api-key` + `api_key="not-used"` to suppress Bearer) to work around an auth issue on `AQ.`-prefix keys. Google has since tightened the `/v1beta/openai` endpoint — sending both headers now returns `API key not valid` even for legacy `AIza…` keys. Your curl header matrix in the comments was the empirical proof; thanks for digging in.

The fix reverts to plain Bearer auth, which Google's OpenAI-compat endpoint accepts for `AIza…` keys. `AQ.`-prefix keys remain broken on this endpoint due to an upstream Google bug (https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/140545) that Google has acknowledged and said they're fixing. Workaround from Google for affected users: regenerate the key in AI Studio to get a non-`AQ` (legacy) key.

Credit to @helix4u (implementation), @alizane (first triage and #12204), and @ciiiii (header matrix proof).

Fix will ship in the next release; `hermes update` will pick it up.

title: [Setup]: Docker volume mounts fail on UnRAID due to USER hermes bypassing entrypoint permission fix
author: rorar
body:
### What's Going Wrong?

Docker container fails to create directories on mounted volumes due to UID mismatch between container user and host volume ownership.

When running Hermes in Docker on UnRAID, volume mounts fail with `Permission denied` errors:

```
mkdir: cannot create directory '/opt/data/cron': Permission denied
mkdir: cannot create directory '/opt/data/sessions': Permission denied
mkdir: cannot create directory '/opt/data/logs': Permission denied
```

The entrypoint never runs `usermod` or `chown` because the container starts as the `hermes` user (UID 10000), not root. The entrypoint relies on `if [ "$(id -u)" = "0" ]` to trigger permission fixes, but this block is bypassed when the container starts as non-root.

### Steps Taken

1. Pulled Hermes Docker image
2. Configured environment variables:
   - `HERMES_UID=99`
   - `HERMES_GID=100`
   - `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`
3. Mounted host volume: `/mnt/user/appdata/hermes-agent:/opt/data`
4. Container starts but cannot write to mounted volume

**Debugging findings:**

```bash
# Container starts with hardcoded UID (not root)
docker inspect hermes-agent | jq '.[0].Config.User'
# → "hermes"

# Hermes runs as UID 10000, volume own

answers.body:

title: [Setup]: WhatsApp bridge npm install timeout too short (60s) on container startup
author: Nicthien
body:
### What's Going Wrong?

Description :
When starting the Hermes container on Unraid (and likely other NAS/slower systems), the WhatsApp bridge fails to install dependencies because the npm install timeout is hardcoded to 60 seconds.

Environment :
- Platform: Unraid (Docker container)
- Hermes version: latest

Error:

[Whatsapp] Installing WhatsApp bridge dependencies...
[Whatsapp] Failed to install dependencies: Command '['npm', 'install', '--silent']' timed out after 60 seconds
[Whatsapp] Disconnecting (external bridge left running)


Location: /opt/hermes/gateway/platforms/whatsapp.py line 387

Suggested fix:
Increase timeout from 60s to 300s (5 minutes), or make it configurable via environment variable.

Workaround:
Manual npm install inside the container after startup:
bash
docker exec -it hermes-agent sh -c 'cd /opt/hermes/scripts/whatsapp-bridge && npm install --verbose'

### Steps Taken

1. Updated Hermes Docker container on Unraid to latest version
2. Container started, WhatsApp bridge attempted to auto-install dependencies
3. npm install timed out after 60 seconds and bridge failed to start

### Installation Method

Docker

### Operating System

Unraid (Docker container)

answers.body:
Thanks for the detailed reports — sharing where this stands and a few diagnostic asks so we can confirm a path forward.

**Status:** On `main`, the WhatsApp bridge `npm install` timeout is now 300s by default and configurable via the `WHATSAPP_NPM_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` env var (in seconds; e.g. `WHATSAPP_NPM_INSTALL_TIMEOUT=900` for 15 minutes). However, @dryas's report above shows 300s isn't always enough, and several of you note the bridge re-installs dependencies on **every** container start — that's a separate root cause (the Docker image isn't pre-baking `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/node_modules`, so the runtime install fires every boot).

To triage further, could affected reporters share:

1. The exact Hermes version inside the container (`docker exec <container> hermes --version`) so we can confirm the timeout fix is present.
2. Whether `WHATSAPP_NPM_INSTALL_TIMEOUT=900` in your compose env unblocks startup, or whether it still times out at the higher ceiling.
3. Output of `docker exec <container> ls /opt/hermes/scripts/whatsapp-bridge/node_modules 2>&1 | head -5` immediately after a fresh container start — this confirms whether `node_modules` is missing on every boot.
4. Whether `/opt/hermes/scripts/whatsapp-bridge/` is on a bind-mount or named volume in your compose file (vs. only inside the image layer).
5. Approximate duration of a successful manual `npm install` inside the container — @MageInt reported ~2 minutes above; a few more data points on slower NAS hardware would h

Fixed on current main: the npm install timeout in the WhatsApp bridge now defaults to **300s** and is configurable via `WHATSAPP_NPM_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` — exactly the suggested fix.

`plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py:544`:
```python
# Read timeout from environment variable, default to 300 seconds (5 minutes)
# to accommodate slower systems like Unraid NAS
npm_install_timeout = env_int("WHATSAPP_NPM_INSTALL_TIMEOUT", 300)
```

(The adapter moved from `gateway/platforms/whatsapp.py` to `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` in the bundled-plugins migration.) Closing as implemented on main.

author: ETIENNECHEN
body:
### Bug Description

Hi all, found something I'd like to cross-check:

Behaviour: When the Claude OAuth is connected to Claude Code CLI, all token consumption is billed as extra usage rather than drawing from my Max plan quota.

Expected: Max plan quota should be consumed first; only overages should count as extra usage.

Questions:
1. Is this just happening to me?
2. Or have I enabled some setting (API key config, billing preference, etc.) that's defaulting it to pay-as-you-go?

If anyone runs the same setup, would appreciate a sanity check. Thanks!

### Steps to Reproduce

.

### Expected Behavior

.

### Actual Behavior

.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell

```

### Operating System

MacOS 26.4.1 

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

answers.body:
Closing — this is intended behavior from Anthropic's side, not a bug we can fix.

Anthropic forces the `mcp_` tool-name prefix as the only pathway through which OAuth subscription tokens (Pro/Max) can access tools at all. The subscription-token tool access they allow is metered against the overage/extra-usage bucket exclusively — there is no "included quota" path for tools on OAuth subscriptions. Removing the prefix doesn't unlock the included quota; it would block all tool-bearing requests on subscription tokens entirely.

The trade-off is intentional: keep the prefix and have tools work for users who have overage enabled (or pay-per-use), or drop the prefix and break tools for every OAuth subscription user. We chose the former.

For Max/Pro subscribers without overage enabled: use an API key instead of the OAuth subscription token, or enable usage-based billing on your Anthropic account.

Tracking issue: #28849.

title: [Question] Can Hermes call arbitrary stdio MCP servers (like Claude Code does)?
author: Motokiyo
body:
## Context

Considering migrating part of my agent stack from Claude Code subagents to Hermes for the persistence + learning loop benefits. My agents currently rely on a local stdio MCP server (MemPalace, a Python knowledge graph) that runs on macOS and is invoked exactly the same way Claude Code invokes any MCP: stdin/stdout JSON-RPC, configured in a settings file.

## Question

Does Hermes support calling arbitrary stdio-based MCP servers as tools, the same way Claude Code does via `mcpServers` config? Or are tool integrations limited to the 40+ built-in tools and HTTP-based MCPs?

Specifically:

1. Is there a config field equivalent to Claude Code's `mcpServers` for declaring custom stdio MCPs?
2. If yes, how does Hermes handle the MCP lifecycle (spawn, stdin/stdout, shutdown) across sessions?
3. Are there platform-specific caveats on macOS (M1, Tahoe 26.2)?

## Why it matters

This is the go/no-go question for migrating my fixed business agents (Galaad / Eiffel AI consultancy) to Hermes. Without arbitrary stdio MCP support, the agents lose access to their shared knowledge graph, which is the backbone of their cross-session memory.

Happy to provide a minimal repro repo of a tes

answers.body:
Yes — Hermes supports arbitrary stdio MCP servers, same shape as Claude Code's `mcpServers`. Top-level `mcp_servers` key in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  mempalace:
    command: python
    args: [-m, mempalace.server]
    env:
      MEMPALACE_DB: /path/to/kg.db
```

Or interactively: `hermes mcp add mempalace --command python --args -m mempalace.server`.

Lifecycle: the gateway spawns your stdio MCP subprocess at startup, keeps one long-lived ClientSession per server, auto-reconnects with backoff if the subprocess dies, and cleans up on shutdown. macOS caveat worth knowing: gateway-under-launchd can have env-inheritance quirks (#14113) that don't show up running `hermes chat` directly — worth testing both paths before cutting over production agents.

Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/cli-commands#mcp  Go/no-go should be green for MemPalace. Closing as answered — reopen if you hit a specific integration snag.

title: Question: does the minute-precision timestamp in `_build_system_prompt` invalidate prompt caching for upstream inference servers?
author: auroter
body:
Running Hermes locally against a `llama-server` instance hosting Qwen3.6-27B, I am seeing repeated catastrophic re-prefill events — `forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data` in the server logs, with checkpoint restoration failing and the divergence in the cached prefix landing at a consistent byte offset. This fires from very early in a session — the cached system prompt alone is enough to trigger it — and gets progressively more painful as conversation history grows; on an M3 Max 64GB I have measured a worst-case 25-minute wall-clock prefill at ~120K context, but the underlying cache invalidation is happening turn-after-turn long before that, just at smaller cost per turn.

Tracing the system-prompt assembly in `run_agent.py`, I think the cause is `_build_system_prompt` at line 4179:

```python
timestamp_line = f"Conversation started: {now.strftime('%A, %B %d, %Y %I:%M %p')}"
```

The `%I:%M %p` format embeds the current minute into the cached system prompt. The docstring on `_build_system_prompt` says it is "called once per session (cached on `self._cached_system_prompt`)", and the gateway path (`api_server.py:_create_agent`) does correctly try to load the sto

answers.body: Yes — the minute-precision timestamp invalidated upstream prefix caching on rebuild paths. Fixed in PR #27675 (merged commit 4a3f13b4): the `Conversation started:` line is now date-only, so the system prompt stays byte-stable for the full day. Thanks for raising the question.

title: RFC: review the Curator — background skill maintenance (PR #16049, closes #7816)
author: teknium1
body:
# Request for review: Curator — background skill maintenance

**PR:** https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/16049
**Original request:** #7816

The Curator is a new auxiliary-model background task (default ON) that periodically reviews **agent-created skills only** — tracks usage, marks long-unused skills stale, archives genuinely obsolete ones, and spawns a forked aux agent to consolidate overlaps and patch drift. Bundled and hub-installed skills are never touched. Archive only — no auto-delete.

Before we merge, we'd like eyes on it from anyone who uses Hermes heavily or has strong opinions on skill lifecycle / ops surfaces. The PR is substantial (~2000 LOC including tests, spanning telemetry, orchestration, CLI, slash command, and gateway integration) and introduces defaults that will affect every user by default.

## The shape at a glance

- **Cadence:** every 7 days (configurable). Piggy-backs on the existing gateway cron ticker so long-running gateways fire on cadence without restarts.
- **Telemetry sidecar:** new `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json` tracks `use_count`, `view_count`, `last_used_at`, `patch_count`, `state`, `pinned`, etc. per agent-created skill.
- **Life

answers.body:
I have some higher-level design concerns here. I like the feature, and I think the deterministic lifecycle part is the right shape: usage tracking, agent-created filtering, stale/archive thresholds, pinning, and reactivation are all handled in code. My concern is the next step: after that lifecycle pass, the curator renders all agent-created skills as a usage-stat candidate list, appends it to a review prompt, and runs a forked `AIAgent(max_iterations=8)` that is instructed to use `skills_list`, `skill_view`, `skill_manage`, and `terminal` to inspect, patch, consolidate, or archive.

That leaves the model doing a lot of discovery work that could be factored into Python first. Before calling a model, I’d rather see the curator compute a small, structured “needs review” list with explicit reasons, such as:

- hash each skill and compare against `last_reviewed_hash` so unchanged skills are skipped
- validate linked files, referenced paths, shell commands, and required env vars
- compute cheap overlap candidates from names, descriptions, triggers, categories, and tool deps
- include the specific reason each candidate needs review

If that list is empty, no model call.

If it’s non-empty, send only that evidence packet to the model and ask for a bounded, structured decision: `keep`, `patch`, `consolidate`, or `archive`. Then have Python execute that decision through narrow code paths: record `keep`, call the existing safe archive function for `archive`, and require `patch` / `cons

Thanks for the detailed RFC — this already answers a lot of the lifecycle questions I had in #7816.

The active → stale → archived flow, the 30d/90d defaults, archive-only behavior, pinning semantics, and restore surface are clear to me.

The one area I’d still love to understand better is the handling of environment-specific claims. The RFC mentions patch drift and lists environment-specific claims as a related concern, but I’m not yet sure whether those claims are revalidated periodically, how the Curator detects them, or what happens when revalidation fails.

Really glad to see this moving forward 🚀🚀🚀

Congrats on the Curator ship! Really nice to see #7816 come to life in v0.12.0.

I had originally opened #7816 requesting skill lifecycle management and also left feedback on this RFC around environment-specific claim validation. I noticed the contributors list in the release notes doesn't include me — I understand contributor credit is typically tied to merged PRs rather than issue discussions, but I wanted to gently flag that the original request and some of the design discussion did come from community input in the issues.

Not making a big deal of it — just wanted to mention it in case there's a way to acknowledge issue authors whose requests shaped a feature. Either way, great to see this shipped!

title: Error code: 400 | "You're out of extra usage. Add more at claude.ai/settings/usage and keep going."
author: ericopent
body: Hi, guys. I've seen old threads (2weeks old) reporting the same error on Hermes with Claude auth. Do we have a solution that does not involve messing up skills, memory? Tks

answers.body: Likely duplicate of #15080. The "out of extra usage" error is an Anthropic billing cap — not a Hermes bug. Existing fix PRs (#11736, #10576) improve how Hermes classifies and handles this error. In the meantime, add credits at claude.ai/settings/usage or use a different provider.

Closing — this is intended behavior from Anthropic's side, not a bug we can fix.

Anthropic forces the `mcp_` tool-name prefix as the only pathway through which OAuth subscription tokens (Pro/Max) can access tools at all. The subscription-token tool access they allow is metered against the overage/extra-usage bucket exclusively — there is no "included quota" path for tools on OAuth subscriptions. Removing the prefix doesn't unlock the included quota; it would block all tool-bearing requests on subscription tokens entirely.

The trade-off is intentional: keep the prefix and have tools work for users who have overage enabled (or pay-per-use), or drop the prefix and break tools for every OAuth subscription user. We chose the former.

For Max/Pro subscribers without overage enabled: use an API key instead of the OAuth subscription token, or enable usage-based billing on your Anthropic account.

Tracking issue: #28849.

title: [Feature]: Dashboard Sessions/Config/Keys tabs need a `?profile=` scope selector so one dashboard process can view & edit per-profile state
author: samplesabotage
body:
### Problem or Use Case

The web dashboard is profile-bound at startup: `hermes dashboard -p <name>` materializes `HERMES_HOME` once, every endpoint reads `state.db`, `config.yaml`, `.env` through `get_hermes_home()` for the lifetime of the process. The Sessions, Config, and Keys tabs therefore only ever show one profile's data, even though the on-disk layout has full per-profile state under `<HERMES_HOME>/profiles/<name>/`.

Operators running multiple profiles in one tenant (single host, single user, several Discord bots / model assignments / personalities) hit this every time they want to:

- See session history for the right profile (the bot they were actually chatting to).
- Rotate a per-profile API key (osaka has its own `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, separate from kyoto's).
- Tweak per-profile `config.yaml` overrides (different model, different toolset).

The current upstream workaround per issue #10674's "interim best practices" is to run *one dashboard process per profile* on different ports — three URLs to remember for three profiles, browser bookmarks proliferating, no unified surface for tenant-scoped concerns (kanban, analytics aggregate, status overview) that already work tenant

author: lhn1194789820
body:
### Bug Description

[agent.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27786938/agent.zip) 
My agent had unexplained deductions. I configured it to use the DeepSeek V4 Flash model, but on the 9th, I discovered it was using the DeepSeek V4 Pro model instead. Since the balance was completely deducted, I just left it alone. Then on the evening of the 14th, I topped up some money, deleted the original model configuration, regenerated the token, and also updated to the latest Hermes agent. I disabled all scheduled tasks, but it still deducted my tokens.

### Steps to Reproduce

Woke up and found it had charged me overnight on its own.

### Expected Behavior


Normally it might only cost a few cents RMB overnight, maybe less than one cent, but even though I didn't do anything, the next day it deducted about 10 RMB.


### Actual Behavior

Normally it might only cost a few cents RMB overnight, maybe less than one cent, but even though I didn't do anything, the next day it deducted about 10 RMB.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug report uploaded:
  Report       https://paste.rs/vAXM8
  agent.log

answers.body:
This is likely caused by the model normalization issue in `hermes_cli/model_normalize.py`. 

**Probable root cause:** `_normalize_for_deepseek()` only recognizes `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` as canonical models. When you configure `deepseek-v4-flash`, it gets force-normalized to `deepseek-chat`, which the DeepSeek API now maps to `deepseek-v4-pro` — a more expensive model.

So the charge discrepancy you're seeing (expecting flash pricing, getting pro pricing) is because Hermes is silently rewriting your model name before sending it to the API.

**Check:** Look at your `agent.log` for lines like:
```
Normalized model 'deepseek-v4-flash' to 'deepseek-chat' for deepseek
```

**Our workaround:** We patched `_DEEPSEEK_CANONICAL_MODELS` in `model_normalize.py` to add `deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-v4-flash` so they pass through unchanged. See my comment on #26269 for the patch details.

Also related: #26269 (TUI still shows `deepseek-chat` which the API no longer accepts).

title: High quota burn with xAI Grok-4.3 OAuth on SuperGrok $30 plan
author: Gatech0
body:
15 min development in Grok-4.3 with a scratch project: 7% of MONTH usage!!!!!

 working before in GPT-5.4 from oAuth OpenAI with real quota with long duration.

oAuth from GROK is NOT a good deal. Is only cheap ads for a dead Model.

answers.body:
Closing — this is an **xAI billing / quota** question, not a Hermes bug.

Hermes doesn't set, meter, or rate-limit xAI usage; we forward your tokens to `api.x.ai/v1/responses` and surface whatever xAI returns. If 15 minutes of grok-4.3 development burned 7% of your monthly quota, the quota size and burn rate are xAI's pricing decisions. Channel feedback via [grok.com support](https://grok.com) or @xAI on X.

If you want to control spend, the configurable knob is on our side:
- Set `agent.reasoning_effort: low` (or `none`) in `config.yaml` to reduce reasoning-token consumption — grok-4.3 with `reasoning_effort=none` still reasons natively server-side but doesn't replay encrypted_content across turns.
- Switch to a cheaper provider for development (Anthropic Claude Sonnet via OAuth, OpenAI gpt-5.4 via Codex OAuth, etc.) and reserve grok-4.3 for high-value queries.

See related context #26847 (Heavy-only quota gating) for the broader picture on standard-SuperGrok limits.

title: [Discussion] 心智孪生体：五层递进蒸馏记忆架构 — 从第一性原理思考 Hermes Memory 的进化
author: shaolin-cloud
body:
# 心智孪生体：从 Hermes Memory 到五层递进蒸馏架构 —— 第一性原理分析与迭代建议

## TL;DR

用 Hermes Agent 从零构建了一个运行在 DeepSeek V4 上的五层记忆系统（L0→L4），80 测试通过，已闭环运行。本文从第一性原理出发，分析当前 Hermes memory 的本质局限，提出基于分层蒸馏的进化路线。

---

## 一、第一性原理：AI Agent 的记忆是什么？

回到本质，问一个问题：

> **如果 Agent 没有 memory，它是什么？**
> 一个无状态的函数：input → output。每次对话都是第一次见你。

> **如果 Agent 有 memory，它应该做到什么？**
> 不是"记住你说过什么"，而是"理解你是谁"。

从这个第一性原理出发，记忆系统有三个本征需求：

```
需求 1: 精确回忆    →  "我上次说的是 Python 还是 Go？"
需求 2: 模式识别    →  "我反复提到'先讨论再执行'，这是一种决策模式"
需求 3: 自我一致    →  "我今天说的不能和三个月前说的矛盾"
```

当前 Hermes memory 工具解决了需求 1，没有解决需求 2 和 3。

---

## 二、当前 Hermes Memory 的架构局限

### 2.1 模型：单层扁平存储

```
conversation → agent 判断重要 → memory.add("一行文本") → inject to system prompt
```

**问题 A：无结构。** "Lin 的家庭成员" 和 "Lin 喜欢 Python" 存在同一个空间，没有任何层级。

**问题 B：无提炼。** 100 条记忆注入 100 条，而不是把 100 条提炼成 5 个核心认知。

**问题 C：无矛盾检测。** "Lin 偏好 Go" 和 "Lin 转向 Python" 同时存在，没有机制识别这是时间演化还是矛盾。

**问题 D：无身份层。** 所有记忆权重相等，没有一个"宪法级"的核心认知。

### 2.2 实证：100 条记忆的困境

```
100 条 memory → ~3000 tokens → 挤占上下文 → agent 决策质量下降
但 100 条中真正有价值的是：
  - 5 条核心认知（Lin 是谁）
  - 20 条偏好约定（说话风格、执行节奏）
  - 75 条状态信息（上一次在做什么、当前项目是什么）
```

前两类是长期价值，第三类会过时。但没有机制区分它们。

---

## 三、心智孪生体：五层递进蒸馏架构

### 3.1 架构

```
L0  原始数据          对话逐字存储 (JSON 文件系统)
    ↓

title: How can two different Hermes isolate their files?
author: bbhxwl
body:
How can two different Hermes isolate their files?
If I use docker as the command running environment and enterprise wechat asks him to send files, he will not really send them successfully.
But if you use local as the command line, their files will be shared with each other again.

answers.body:
**Two supported ways to run multiple, fully-isolated Hermes agents:**

**1. Built-in profiles (recommended)**

Hermes has first-class multi-agent support via *profiles* — each profile is a separate namespace (its own `config.yaml`, `SOUL.md`, sessions, memories, skills, credentials) under `profiles/<name>/`, with no file sharing between them.

```sh
hermes profile create work
hermes profile create personal
hermes profile list
hermes profile use work          # set a sticky default
hermes --profile personal chat   # or select per-invocation
```

You can also select a profile via the `HERMES_PROFILE` environment variable (e.g. `HERMES_PROFILE=personal hermes ...`), which is handy for gateways/containers. Each profile can run its own supervised gateway, so two agents on different platforms stay completely separate.

**2. Separate `HERMES_HOME` directories**

If you'd rather keep them in entirely distinct trees (e.g. different volumes/containers), point each agent at its own home dir with the `HERMES_HOME` env var:

```sh
HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes-work     hermes gateway run
HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes-personal hermes gateway run
```

Everything (config, keys, sessions, skills, memory) lives under that directory, so the two installs share nothing. In Docker, just mount a different host dir to `/opt/data` per container.

---

On the file-sharing behaviour you saw: with `terminal.backend: local`, tool subprocesses run in your shared host filesystem, so two agents *can* see each other's files

title: [Discussion] Why was smart_model_routing removed? Request to restore
author: CharmLynn
body:
## Background

The `smart_model_routing` feature was added in March 2026 (commit 4b0056159) and removed a month later in April (commit 424e9f36b, PR #12732).

This feature auto-routed short/simple turns (≤160 chars or ≤28 words) to a cheaper model, saving costs for trivial queries like "hello", "thanks", etc.

## Question

The commit message says it was "opt-in and disabled by default" but doesn't explain why it was removed wholesale instead of keeping it as an opt-in feature.

**Could you share the reasoning behind this decision?**

## User Impact

Many users find this feature useful for cost optimization:
- Simple greetings/acknowledgments don't need expensive models
- Config was `smart_model_routing.enabled: true` with `cheap_model: opencode-zen/deepseek-v4-flash-free`
- Saved tokens for trivial turns while keeping strong model for real work

## Request

1. If there were technical issues, could they be fixed instead of removing?
2. If there's a better alternative, please document it
3. Consider restoring this feature as opt-in (or with improved routing logic)

## Current Workaround

Users can manually switch models:
```bash
hermes chat -m opencode-zen/deepseek-v4-flash-free
```

- Hermes does not accept complexity-based automatic model routing, cheap-vs-strong model tiers, or per-turn/per-task provider-model overrides.
- The requested restoration of `smart_model_routing` is exactly that policy category. The prior implementation was deliberately removed in 424e9f36b, and current CLI and gateway route resolution explicitly retain the session's primary model/provider.
- The linked discussion is part of the same routing cluster; related issue #20249 was closed under this policy with the same scope.
- The supported configuration point for subagents remains `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` in `config.yaml`. Manual `/model` selection and focused fixes to existing switching or fallback behavior remain separate, valid topics.

body:
### What's Going Wrong?

User: Kelly Hess
     Setup: Hermes Agent v0.14.0 running on WSL2 (Ubuntu)
     Primary access method: Telegram bot @anniemaebot
     Secondary method attempted: Web UI on port 8787
     Problem 1: Telegram – "Unauthorized user"

     - User ID 6614365140 (Kelly Hess) is being rejected with:
       WARNING gateway.run: Unauthorized user: 6614365140 (Kelly Hess)
     on telegram
     - Tried the following in ~/.hermes/config.yaml:
       - allowed_chats: '6614365140'
       - allowed_chats: '' + guest_mode: true
     - Neither setting resolved the issue. The gateway continued to
     block the user even after multiple restarts (hermes gateway restart
     and systemctl --user restart).
     - Running the gateway manually (python -m hermes_cli.main gateway
     run) produced the same error.
     Problem 2: Web UI – Persistent password prompt

     - Web UI (bootstrap.py) keeps asking for a password even after:
       - Setting HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD=letmein in .env
       - Deleting ~/.hermes/webui/.pbkdf2_key, .signing_key,
     .login_attempts.json, and .sessions.json
       - Running rm -rf ~/.hermes/webui/*
       - Starting with python3 bootstrap.py --hos

answers.body:
Hi Kelly — both issues come down to using the wrong config key / wrong component. Here's the breakdown.

## Problem 1: Telegram "Unauthorized user"

`allowed_chats` is **not** the user-authorization key — that's why it had no effect. It's a *group-chat response whitelist* (when set, the bot only responds in those group chat IDs). It does not authorize a DM user.

User authorization is checked by `_is_user_authorized()`, which looks at (in order):
1. Per-platform allow-all flag — `TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`
2. Per-platform allowlist — `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` (config key `allow_from`)
3. DM pairing-approved list
4. Global allow-all — `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`
5. Default: deny

`guest_mode: true` also won't help here — it only permits **group** messages that explicitly @mention the bot; it does nothing for DMs.

### Fix — pick one

**Option A — allowlist your user ID (recommended):**
```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
telegram:
  allow_from: "6614365140"     # comma-separated for multiple users
```
(Internally this sets `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`.)

**Option B — pairing flow:** DM the bot, it replies with a pairing code, then on the host run:
```
hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>
```

**Option C — allow everyone (only if you trust the bot's reachability):**
```yaml
telegram:
  allow_all: true              # sets TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS
```

Restart the gateway after editing config: `hermes gateway restart`.

body:
### What's Going Wrong?

Anyone managed to configure asana MCP properly
https://developers.asana.com/docs/connecting-mcp-clients-to-asanas-v2-server#1-prerequisites-3

I have added the following in my config.yaml

```

  asana:
    url: "https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp"
    auth: oauth
    oauth:                     
      client_id: "xxxxxx"
      client_secret: "xxxxx"
      redirect_uri: "http://127.0.0.1:38389/callback"
```


After I pasted the code, it says

> Got authorization code from paste — completing flow


But it loops through again shows url ( https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize), after some time it say

>   ✗ Authentication failed: MCP call timed out after 40.0s (configured timeout: 40.0s)



### Steps Taken

1. configure config.yaml
2. then ran "hermes mcp login asana"

### Installation Method

Install script (curl | bash)

### Operating System

Ubuntu

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)

### Debug Report

```shell

```

### Full Error Output

```shell
hermes mcp login asana

  Starting OAuth flow for 'asana'...

  MCP OAuth: authorization required.
  Open this URL in your browser:

    https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_auth

answers.body:
Thanks for the detailed report — this is a known issue with the OAuth login flow.

**Root cause:** `hermes mcp login` wraps the entire OAuth flow inside a 40-second timeout (`connect_timeout=30` + 10s buffer), but the browser authorization step — where you paste the code — needs more time. When the timeout fires mid-flow, it can cause the re-authorization loop you're seeing before ultimately failing with the timeout error.

This is tracked in **#24097** (same bug, different server). The fix PRs are in review:

- **#50458** — extends the OAuth login timeout to 300s for interactive flows
- **#51149** — fixes an auth-lock issue that can cause the re-authorization loop on Streamable HTTP connections
- **#34276** — honors per-server `connect_timeout` from config.yaml

**Workaround for now:** Use SSH port forwarding so the redirect is captured automatically, bypassing the paste-and-timeout path:

```
# In a separate terminal:
ssh -N -L 39575:127.0.0.1:39575 <user>@<your-host>

# Then run the login — the redirect will be received by the local listener:
hermes mcp login asana
```

This avoids the interactive paste fallback entirely. Once any of the fix PRs lands, `hermes mcp login` should work without the port forward.

<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=36725 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->
Thanks for the detailed OAuth trace. This is now fixed on `main` by the same timeout issue identified in the prior discussion; this is an automated hermes-sweeper review.

- Merged PR #59219 (`f26ae4f6830d0ced54ab61cd1ef03b35fadb3f91`) changed `hermes mcp login` to honor a server's configured `connect_timeout` and enforce a 315-second interactive OAuth floor.
- `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py:787-802` now passes that timeout into the login probe, replacing the former 30-second probe / 40-second total failure path.
- The linked tracking issue #24097 was closed by #59219, and the current OAuth-over-SSH guide documents pasted redirects for Asana-class MCP servers.
- The fix is included in release tag `v2026.7.7`.

title: [Setup]: Hermes Gateway Scheduled Task shows visible cmd window on Windows — with fix
author: OmarElsewefi
body:
### What's Going Wrong?

Hi Hermes Agent team,

I'm on Windows 11 (git-bash/MSYS) and after `hermes gateway install`, the Telegram gateway works, but a visible cmd.exe window stays on screen. Closing it disconnects the gateway.

### The problem
The Scheduled Task runs `Hermes_Gateway.cmd` → `pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run`. Even though pythonw.exe is GUI-subsystem, the parent `cmd.exe` creates a visible console window that stays open.

schtasks with `<HideAppWindow>` isn't supported in Schema v1.2. Attempting `schtasks /Delete` or `Unregister-ScheduledTask` returns Access Denied.



### Steps Taken

### The fix
Replace the direct pythonw.exe call with a PowerShell hidden launcher in the .cmd wrapper:

```cmd
@echo off
powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -NoProfile -Command ^
    "Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden" ^
    " -FilePath 'C:\...\pythonw.exe'" ^
    " -ArgumentList '-m','hermes_cli.main','gateway','run';"
exit /b 0
```

Pipeline: `Scheduled Task → cmd.exe → PowerShell Hidden → Start-Process Hidden → pythonw.exe` — zero windows.

### Suggestion for devs
Update `hermes_cli/gateway_windows.py` (`_build_gateway_cmd_script()`) to generate the PowerShell hidden patte

answers.body:
Consolidated into the Windows console-window-flash tracking issue #54220.

That tracker has the full code-verified map of which subprocess spawn sites are still leaking on current `main`, the fix attempts we tried and **reverted** (so we don't repeat the red herrings), and a targeted fix plan. Your report is captured there. Thanks for the detail — it fed directly into the root-cause analysis.

title: [Setup]: OpenRouter credential configured but Hermes sends requests without Authentication header
author: HermitRobot
body:
### What's Going Wrong?

I am trying to use Hermes with OpenRouter on macOS.

Hermes Desktop launches successfully and Hermes CLI starts normally. OpenRouter is selected as the provider and the model is set to `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`.

However, every chat request fails with:

`HTTP 401: Missing Authentication header`

The same API key works successfully outside Hermes using a direct Python/OpenRouter smoke test, so the provider, model access, network connectivity, and API key appear to be valid.

The issue appears to be that Hermes is not attaching an Authorization header to OpenRouter requests.

### Steps Taken

1. Installed Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) on macOS (Mac mini M1).
2. Installed and launched Hermes Desktop.
3. Selected OpenRouter as the provider.
4. Selected model `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`.
5. Verified direct OpenRouter access using the same API key via a standalone Python smoke test.
6. Ran:

```bash
hermes chat -q "Reply with exactly: Hermes auth fixed"
```

7. Also tested through Hermes Desktop with the same result.

### Installation Method

Install script (curl | bash)

### Operating System

MacOS 26.1

### Python Version

3.11.15

answers.body:
Fixed in PR #42263 (merged to main, commit 9c9d911).

Root cause: `resolve_provider()` auto-detection only checked the `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` env vars, never the credential pool. A key added via `hermes auth add openrouter` lives in the pool with no env var, so it was invisible — the provider resolved with an empty api_key and requests went out with no `Authorization` header, which OpenRouter reports as `HTTP 401: Missing Authentication header` (distinct from an *invalid* key). That also explains why `hermes auth list` showed the credential while the debug dump read `openrouter not set` — the dump only inspected env vars too.

The fix makes auto-detection consult the OpenRouter pool, and `hermes debug share` now prints `openrouter set (auth pool)` when the key lives in the pool instead of the misleading `not set`.

After updating (`hermes update`), a credential added via `hermes auth add openrouter` will be picked up without needing `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env`. Thanks for the detailed debug report — the `Missing Authentication header` vs `auth list shows it` mismatch pointed straight at the gap.

title: Question: preferred contribution path for an aX platform adapter?
author: madtank
body:
Hi Hermes maintainers — before preparing an upstream PR, we wanted to ask whether this is an option you would be open to, and what contribution path would be most useful for this repo.

We think aX may make sense alongside Hermes because Hermes already has a platform-adapter architecture for long-running agents, and aX is an agent-native collaboration/activity layer for addressability, presence/status, spaces, mention wake/routing, durable task/context continuity, and MCP-backed capabilities.

The contribution we are imagining is intentionally small: a thin platform adapter for message delivery, presence/status, mention wake/routing, threading, and recovery. Richer capabilities would stay outside the adapter via MCP, so the adapter would not introduce a second tool stack.

We have kept the prototype/proof small and scoped, and can share a branch or patch once the preferred route is clear. We want to avoid guessing at Hermes conventions.

Would you prefer one of these paths?

1. Small platform-adapter/plugin PR
2. Example integration
3. Docs/demo recipe
4. Initial design/protocol/security issue
5. Another venue or route, such as Discord or a maintainer-preferred channel

Any adapter

answers.body:
<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=42473 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->
Thanks for checking the contribution path before preparing a PR. This automated hermes-sweeper review found that current main already documents the recommended path for this exact kind of community platform adapter.

- The recommended route is a standalone platform plugin in `~/.hermes/plugins/`, rather than a core integration: `website/docs/developer-guide/adding-platform-adapters.md:9-13,31-39`.
- The guide covers the adapter contract, `ctx.register_platform()` registration, configuration and authorization hooks, multi-profile token locks, and reference implementations: `website/docs/developer-guide/adding-platform-adapters.md:21-29,117-147,174-199,455-457`.
- The guide was introduced in commit `289d2745afd2dc9ae881d0b873371bfb0eb7b228` (`docs: add platform adapter developer guide + WeCom Callback docs`).

Please use that plugin path and its referenced IRC/Teams/Google Chat/LINE examples when preparing the adapter; richer capabilities can remain outside the adapter as described in the issue.

author: nnnarvaez
body:
#### TL | DR

Fallback for both `_OPENROUTER_MODEL` and `_NOUS_MODEL` are hardcoded to `gemini-3-flash-preview`.



I do local inference with QWEN but wanted to try their free Gemma4 and added my openrouter key to my .env

```

```
So hermes is defaulting to Gemini 3 Flash Preview a paid model to generate session titles, even if the price is not high there is no reason to default to a paid model for such a silly task when the openrouter key is provided to hermes. 

I know people don't care and spend thousands of dollars in inference, but if i am providing local inference as a main model it would stand to reason to expect that silly tasks would not default to a paid service. 


```
Fallback chain (openrouter → nous → local/custom → api-key)
```


```
Looking at the code flow, when 'provider: auto'is set, it calls '_resolve_auto()'

answers.body: Duplicate of #24029 — same root cause: `auxiliary_client.py` hardcodes `_OPENROUTER_MODEL`/`_NOUS_MODEL` to the paid `google/gemini-3-flash-preview`, so auxiliary tasks (session title generation, etc.) bill a paid OpenRouter model even when your main provider is local/free. Tracked there alongside fix discussion (#24039, #25180).

Fixed on `main` by PR #47235 ("fix(auxiliary): honor fallback policy for auto tasks", merged in commit 4858942c).

You correctly identified the root cause: `_OPENROUTER_MODEL` / `_NOUS_MODEL` (`google/gemini-3-flash-preview`) was a hardcoded auxiliary default reached whenever the main provider failed, regardless of the user's configured fallback policy.

`_resolve_auto()` now consults user fallback policy **before** that hardcoded discovery chain:

1. `auxiliary.<task>.fallback_chain`
2. top-level `fallback_providers` / `fallback_model`
3. only then the built-in `openrouter → nous → custom → api-key` discovery defaults

So for local-inference / custom-endpoint users (the exact case you described), auxiliary tasks now route through your declared fallback policy instead of jumping to the hardcoded Gemini default. Thanks for the digging and the cross-reference to #24029.

title: Design question: should AGENTS.md walk parents like .hermes.md does?
author: gdeyoung
body:
## Question: Should `AGENTS.md` discovery walk parents like `.hermes.md` does?

### Context

I noticed a documentation asymmetry in how Hermes loads project context files (`agent/prompt_builder.py`):

| File | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `.hermes.md` / `HERMES.md` | Walks parents up to git root, stops at git root |
| `AGENTS.md` / `agents.md` | **Cwd only** — subdirectory and parent copies are ignored |

This is intentional, codified by an existing test (`test_agents_md_top_level_only` in `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py`), and probably correct for most users. **I'm not reporting a bug — I'm asking whether there's a use case worth addressing.**

### Use cases I've seen for hierarchical `AGENTS.md`

1. **Monorepos** with a root `AGENTS.md` describing repo-wide rules (style, test policy) and per-package `AGENTS.md` for package-specific rules.
2. **Nested worktrees** where the outer worktree has rules and the inner worktree extends them.
3. **Symlinking or aliasing** a shared `AGENTS.md` from a higher-level docs directory.

For all three, users currently work around it by pasting the root `AGENTS.md` content into the per-directory file (drift), or by relying on `.hermes.md` (Hermes-spec

<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->

title: Question: smarter truncation strategy for context files (74% of project's own AGENTS.md gets dropped)
author: gdeyoung
body:
## Question: Should `_truncate_content` (and friends) use a smarter strategy than head/tail?

### The data point

The 69,200-char `AGENTS.md` that ships with `hermes-agent` itself (the contribution-rubric file at the repo root) is being silently truncated to 18,099 chars when an agent runs from the project directory. That's **74% of the file dropped** in the middle.

1. The model has no way to know *which* part was cut. A `read_file` on the whole 69K file re-injects it all, defeating the original purpose of the cap.
2. For project context, the model often *doesn't* realize i

This looks like a broken/partial install rather than a source bug. On current `main`, `init_agent()` in `agent/agent_init.py` accepts `event_callback`, and its caller in `run_agent.py` passes it — the two are in sync. They were added together atomically in commit `e76e7b50` ("feat(hooks): session:compress event_callback for MemPalace sync"), which touched both files in the same commit, so there was never a released state where the caller passed a kwarg the signature didn't accept.

That points to your installed tree being mismatched — e.g. `hermes update` updated `run_agent.py` but left an older `agent/agent_init.py` (or a stale `hermes-agent` package / `__pycache__` shadowing the new one). A clean reinstall should clear it:

```
pip uninstall hermes-agent    # if installed as a package
# then re-run the installer, or: find . -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +
```

If it persists after a clean reinstall on the latest `main`, please reopen with the output of `hermes --version` and the full traceback (the exact unexpected kwarg name) and I'll take another look.

title: Opt-in progress notice during long auto-compression pauses? (compression is silent by design today)
author: havok-training
body:
### Problem or Use Case

On long sessions, auto-compression (session hygiene) can pause the turn for tens
of seconds while the summarization model runs. During that window the gateway is
silent, so on a chat platform (Telegram, etc.) it looks like the bot stalled or
ignored the message. A user running big sessions has no signal that the pause is
expected.

I see this is **intentional today** — `test_session_hygiene_messages_stay_in_originating_topic`
asserts `len(adapter.sent) == 0` with the note *"Compression warnings are no
longer sent to users — compression happens silently with server-side logging
only."* So I want to ask before proposing code, rather than reverse a deliberate
decision.

### Proposed Solution

An **opt-in, default-OFF** progress notice: when enabled, send a short "compressing
session…" message on compression start and a "compressed: N→M messages" message on
completion. Default behavior stays exactly as today (silent), so the existing
regression test and the current UX are unchanged. Strings would go through the
`t()` i18n catalog like other gateway messages.

This mirrors how the opt-in Telegram stop button (#15954) is gated behind a flag
to avoid changing defa

answers.body:
Implemented on main via PR #70457 (merge 4025329ac4) — built to your exact design, @havok-training: opt-in `compression.progress_notices` (default OFF), silent default preserved byte-for-byte, existing regression tests untouched. When enabled, routine compression statuses (start / preflight / idle-resume) AND the completion stat pass the gateway noise filter to chat platforms; everything else stays suppressed.

Implementation note: since your issue was filed, every routine compression status became a template constant emitted at the right moments (#69550) — so the feature reduced to a config gate on the noise filter rather than new emit sites, which is why we built it directly rather than round-tripping the design discussion. Your framing (opt-in, default-off, alternatives analysis, respecting the silent-by-design test) made this an easy yes — thanks for asking first and asking well. Design credit is in the PR body.

title: Bug: Pasting Chinese/CJK into Web Dashboard produces ??? due to PowerShell ANSI code page
author: zhigaodihuang
body:
## Platform

Windows 11, WSL2, Hermes Web Dashboard and Desktop app

## Description

Pasting Chinese/CJK text from the Windows clipboard into the Hermes Web Dashboard or Desktop app produces literal `???` instead of the actual characters.

Example: pasting `你好世界，测试中文` results in `????????????`.

## Root cause

The clipboard read path in `ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts` uses `powershell.exe Get-Clipboard -Raw` with `-NoProfile`, which bypasses the user's PowerShell profile. PowerShell then outputs clipboard content using the system ANSI code page (CP936 on Chinese Windows), not UTF-8.

When Hermes reads with `encoding: 'utf8'`, it interprets ANSI-coded bytes as UTF-8, and bytes that don't form valid UTF-8 are replaced with `?`.

Affects ALL non-ASCII characters on non-UTF-8 Windows locales: CJK, emoji, accented characters (e, u, n), Cyrillic, etc.

## The fix already exists on the write path

In the same file (`clipboard.ts`), the **write** direction (lines 102-103) already solves the identical problem for `Set-Clipboard` using base64 + `UTF8.GetString`. But the **read** direction is still broken.

## Suggested fix

In `ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts`, line 6, change:
```
const POWERSHELL

answers.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Duplicate of #38077 — same root cause (read-path `Get-Clipboard -Raw` under `-NoProfile` emits the system ANSI codepage, decoded as UTF-8). #38077 covers the emoji variant; this is the CJK variant of the identical bug, same file/line (`ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts`). The read-path fix is in flight as PR #37212 (mirrors the already-merged write-path fix #35222).
