answers.body:
Reinstall is the fix here — this is an environment breakage on your box, not a defect in the install path.

`uv trampoline failed to spawn Python child process / Caused by: entity not found (os error 2)` means the `hermes.exe` launcher is still on your PATH but the Python interpreter it points at — `venv\Scripts\python.exe` inside the Hermes install — no longer exists (deleted, moved, or a half-finished/partial install). On a clean PowerShell-installer run, `hermes.exe` references the venv's own python sitting right next to it, so nothing we ship can orphan it; once that interpreter is gone the venv is gone, and a reinstall is the only recovery.

Two things worth noting from the report:
- Install method is listed as "curl | bash" on Windows 11, but our `install.sh` hard-refuses on Windows and tells you to use the PowerShell installer — so that path never produced a working install. Use the PowerShell one-liner below.
- This is the same root cause already triaged in #54979 and #48763 (both closed as cannot-reproduce).

**Recommended — clean reinstall (PowerShell):**

```powershell
cd $env:USERPROFILE
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes
iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)
```

The `cd $env:USERPROFILE` first matters — Windows refuses to delete a directory any shell is `cd`'d inside, and `-Recurse -Force` can leave a broken skeleton behind otherwise.

title: Telegram messages disappearing due to deduplication?
author: BWGgit
body:
The log sequence per turn:
1. Response is streamed via Flushing text batch calls (multiple chunks)
2. By the time the agent finishes generating, content_delivered=True because streaming already pushed the content
3. The "normal final send" is suppressed as a duplicate
4. The macOS client briefly renders the streamed message, then removes it

Not affected
- Messages that complete before streaming threshold (short/fast responses) — these stick normally
- Intermediate/polling messages (like "checking..." or clarifying questions) — these also stick
- Other Telegram clients may or may not exhibit the same issue (only macOS Desktop confirmed)

Likely root cause
The Telegram platform adapter's streaming implementation sends partial content as it's generated, then when the response is fully ready, suppresses the final delivery as a duplicate. The macOS Desktop client appears to interpret the streamed-content-then-suppression cycle as a deletion or replacement, removing the visible message.

Ensure the streamed delivery properly finalizes/commits the message on completion rather than suppressing the final send entirely, or send a dedicated "message finalized" signal t

title: **Web dashboard: clicking a previous session opens a blank new session (`/api/pty` `?attach=` reattach discards the `?resume=` spawn env)**
author: Axmr1
body:
### Bug Description

In the web dashboard, clicking any previous session (sidebar SESSIONS list, or Sessions -> History -> "Resume in Chat") opens an empty new session instead of resuming the transcript. Only the first session clicked after a dashboard restart resumes correctly; every later click lands back on that same PTY. No data is lost, the sessions are intact in state.db, the dashboard just never attaches to them.

This is the web/ half of the session-resume family that #55578 fixed for the desktop app (8e734810d touched apps/desktop only; the web dashboard path was missed).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the dashboard and open the chat page once (this creates the keep-alive PTY).
2. Go to Sessions -> History and click the play icon ("Resume in Chat") on any old session, or click a previous session in the sidebar.
3. The chat shows a blank new session instead of the clicked session's transcript.
4. Restart the dashboard process and repeat: now the FIRST clicked session resumes correctly, and every subsequent click again lands on that session's PTY regardless of which session was clicked.

### Expected Behavior

I click previous session, previous session is presented...

##

answers.body:
Thanks @Axmr1 — this is the same root cause as #61284, and your analysis nails it independently.

Both come down to the `/api/pty` keep-alive registry keying **only** on the per-browser `attach` token, so `attach_or_spawn(attach_token, …)` reattaches to the living PTY and throws away the freshly-built `HERMES_TUI_RESUME` env. Same regression lineage (`e10e4bca8`, 0.18.0→0.18.2), same "exactly one resume per dashboard restart" tell.

There's an open PR for it: **#60745**. It takes the same approach you proposed — namespacing the keep-alive identity by the requested resume target — just a bit more complete:

- your patch: `attach_token = f"{attach_token}::{_explicit_resume}"`
- #60745: folds **both** profile and the raw resume into a composite key, `f"{attach_token}\0{profile or ''}\0{raw_resume or ''}"`, and keys on `raw_resume` captured **before** the active-session-file fallback so plain default-`/chat` refresh keep-alive still coalesces.

So your "namespace by resume target" instinct is exactly right; #60745 just also covers the profile axis and the default-`/chat` edge.

This looks like a duplicate of #61284 — the fix is tracked in #60745 (flagging for a maintainer to link/close as they see fit). @Axmr1 if you're running your local patch, #60745 should let you drop it once it lands (no more re-patching after `hermes update`). Worth a review/thumbs-up on the PR if you have a minute, since you've clearly reproduced this end to end.

The root cause here — the `/api/pty` keep-alive registry keying only on the per-browser `attach` token, so a reattach discarded the freshly built `HERMES_TUI_RESUME` env — was fixed by PR #60745 (merged Jul 16, credit @rayjun): the registry key is now the composite `attach\0profile\0resume-target`, so a `?resume=<id>` connection can never coalesce onto a PTY spawned for a different target. The parent→canonical-child variant flagged in review is covered too — the key uses the resolved `HERMES_TUI_RESUME` identity (`registry_resume`), not the raw parent id.

Two follow-ups since have fixed what the reattach bug was masking:
- PR #86332 — the dashboard now requests a full TUI redraw (Ctrl-L) when reusing a keep-alive PTY, so reconnects to long sessions repaint the transcript instead of showing only the recent status rows
- PR #86375 — resumed sessions follow the PTY replay to the bottom of the terminal

Closing as fixed on main. If clicking a previous session still opens a blank new session on a current build (>= the Jul 16 fix), please reopen with the `hermes --version` and the `/api/pty` query string from devtools.

body:
### What's Going Wrong?

I ran the Hermes-Setup.exe (Desktop App with GUI) which i downloaded from the official website, when i open it, it gives an error, I think there is an error with the install.ps1 script at line 1619 specifically.

### Steps Taken

1. Ran Hermes-Setup.exe
2. Clicked "Install Hermes"
3. Error Appears

### Installation Method

PowerShell installer (Windows)

### Operating System

Windows 10

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

n/a

### Debug Report

```shell

```

### Full Error Output

```shell
2026-07-18T15:22:39.932887Z  INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib: Hermes installer starting mode=Install force_setup=false
2026-07-18T15:22:42.268537Z  INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib::bootstrap: bootstrap starting pin=Pin { commit: None, branch: Some("main") } kind=Ps1 include_desktop=true
2026-07-18T15:22:42.269949Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [bootstrap] downloading install.ps1 for main from GitHub
2026-07-18T15:22:43.302134Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [bootstrap] cached to C:\Users\aarsh\AppData\Local\hermes\bootstrap-cache\install-main.ps1
2026-07-18T15:22:43.302155Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [bootstrap] script C:\Users\aarsh\AppData\Local\hermes\bootstrap-cache\install-main.ps1 via do

answers.body:
Opened https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/67021 to fix this.

Root cause: `scripts/install.ps1` has no UTF-8 BOM, and a recent commit put two non-ASCII characters (a bullet `•` and an em-dash `—`) *inside* two `Write-Host`/`Write-Info` string literals. Windows PowerShell 5.1 — which the bootstrap runs the cached script under — reads a BOM-less `.ps1` in the system ANSI code page (CP1252), not UTF-8. The em-dash's tail byte decodes to a smart close-quote (U+201D) that PowerShell treats as a string delimiter, prematurely closing the string and desyncing the parser — which is why you see the unrelated errors at lines 1619/1770. (Deleting the AppData\hermes folder doesn't help because the same file is re-downloaded and re-parsed each time.)

The PR converts the file to pure ASCII (em-dash → `--`, bullet → `-`) so it can't be misdecoded under any code page, and adds a regression test locking that invariant.

answers.body:
Fix submitted in PR #69366.

**Root cause**: The `2>&1 | Out-Null` on the astral uv installer command was suppressing ALL output, including errors. When the installer failed (download, permissions, etc.), users saw only the generic "uv installed but not found" message with no context.

**Fix**: Removed the output suppression so the installer's progress and errors flow through to the terminal. On failure, users will now see the actual error from the astral installer (e.g., "failed to download binaries", "access denied", etc.), making it possible to diagnose and resolve the issue.

I'd like to take this. Plan: investigate the `uv.exe` detection path in `scripts/install.ps1` — the astral installer may place `uv.exe` in a different location than `$HermesHome\bin\` on some Windows configurations. Will add a post-install search/fallback and open a PR.

Fixed in #86727 (merged).

Thanks @BitBernd for the report, @gakugaku for the corporate-proxy diagnosis that motivated the GitHub fallback, and @webtecnica for first identifying the `Out-Null` output suppression in #69366.

`Install-Uv` in `scripts/install.ps1` now climbs a three-rung ladder instead of failing silently:

1. **astral.sh installer** — output is now captured (`Tee-Object`) instead of piped to `Out-Null`, so real errors (download blocked, AV quarantine, permissions) reach you.
2. **GitHub releases mirror** — if astral.sh leaves no `uv.exe` (e.g. blocked by a corporate proxy), the byte-identical installer at `https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-installer.ps1` is tried with the same `UV_INSTALL_DIR`. The script logs which source succeeded.
3. **Salvage an existing uv** — if both installers fail but a working `uv.exe` exists (`Get-Command uv` or `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\uv.exe`), it is copied into `%USERPROFILE%\.hermes\bin\uv.exe` and verified with `--version`.

Only if all three rungs fail do you now see the error — and it includes the last 15 lines of installer output plus the manual-install pointer, so the generic "uv installed but not found" dead end is gone.

author: strohjarvis
body:
# Bug: `auth_middleware` rejects the desktop `/api/ws?token=...` upgrade with HTTP 401

## Affected version
hermes-agent `0.20.0` (install stamp `fa83af3f9a42`, main, local install).
Reproduced on macOS arm64.

## Symptom
The Electron desktop app fails to boot in a loop:

```
Local Hermes backend is HTTP-reachable but the WebSocket (/api/ws) rejected the session token: WebSocket connection failed.
→ Desktop boot failed → Restarting
```

## Root cause
`apps/desktop/dist/electron-main.mjs` spawns the backend with:

```
serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
```

and opens the WebSocket upgrade at `/api/ws?token=<session_token>` (the
desktop app's own freshly minted token, set as `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN`
in the backend child env).

The backend's `auth_middleware`
(`hermes_cli/web_server.py`, `auth_middleware`) gates **every** `/api/*`
request:

```python
if path.startswith("/api/") and path not in _PUBLIC_API_PATHS and not is_mcp_oauth_callback:
    if not _has_valid_session_token(request) and not _has_valid_query_token(request, path):
        return JSONResponse(status_code=401, ...)
```

`_has_valid_query_token` only whitelists `/api/files/download` for the
`?token=` query param —

answers.body:
<!-- hermes-autotriage -->
<!-- action=diagnosis-correction issue=85496 at=2026-08-13T17:58Z -->

I dug into this and I think the proposed middleware fix, while it patches a real inconsistency, won't actually resolve the desktop boot loop — because the desktop's `/api/ws` handshake never reaches `auth_middleware`. Wanted to flag that before anyone lands "exempt WS paths in the middleware," since that would weaken the HTTP-layer check without fixing the reported symptom.

**What I could reproduce (a real, but separate, bug).** In loopback mode, an *HTTP* request to a WS path with a valid token is wrongly rejected, because `_has_valid_query_token` only whitelists `/api/files/download`:

```
GET /api/ws              -> 401   (expected)
GET /api/ws?token=<valid_SESSION_TOKEN> -> 401   (bug: valid token rejected)
```

And this is whole-class, not just `/api/ws`: all six `@app.websocket("/api/…")` routes — `ws`, `pty`, `pub`, `console`, `events`, `audio/speak-stream` — authenticate via `_ws_auth_ok`, so all of them 401 a valid `?token=` at the HTTP layer.

answers.body:
**Same issue here — resolved with `--use-system-ca`**

I'm experiencing the exact same error chain on Windows:

1. `get-windows@9.3.0` prebuilt binary download fails: `unable to verify the first certificate`
2. Falls back to `node-gyp` source compilation
3. Fails because no Visual Studio / Build Tools installed

**Environment**
- OS: Windows 11 (Build 26200)
- Node.js: v22.23.2 (bundled with Hermes)
- Hermes Agent: v0.20.1
- No Visual Studio Build Tools installed

**Root cause**
Node.js cannot verify GitHub's SSL certificate when downloading the `get-windows` prebuilt binary. The error message itself hints at the fix:
> `unable to verify the first certificate; if the root CA is installed locally, try running Node.js with --use-system-ca`

**Solution**
Set `NODE_OPTIONS` to use the system CA store before running `hermes desktop`:

```powershell
$env:NODE_OPTIONS="--use-system-ca"
hermes desktop
```

**Result**
- `get-windows` prebuilt binary downloaded successfully (no compilation needed)
- `added 1290 packages in 1m`
- Desktop app built and packaged successfully
- **No Visual Studio Build Tools installation required**

This appears to be a Node.js certificate verification issue rather than a missing build tools problem. The prebuilt binary for Windows x64 exists and works fine once the SSL handshake succeeds.
